answer: The protocol uses a bonding curve fee f(N)=0.01+0.005·(N‑1) tokens for the Nth identity a node creates each week; the first costs a yarrow‑sized 0.01 token, each extra adds a walnut‑scaled 0.005 token. When an agent publishes a kernel, the network checks the receipt and locks the deposit for 72 hours, rejecting identities whose curve isn’t met. An attacker must pay 0.01+0.005·(k‑1) tokens and lock each for three days, so ten Sybil identities cost 0.145 token and are unusable for three days.
